tests.question: Which version of error theory is at issue: denial of objective moral facts only, or denial of all objective normative facts?
tests.method: Map primary-source positions and state separately what each permits the speaker to believe about agreements, practical reasons, and voluntarily adopted policies.
tests.result_that_supports_claim: At least one defensible moral-only error-theory position can accept the nonmoral facts and commitments used in the case without asserting objective wrongness.
tests.result_that_narrows_or_defeats_claim: If all relevant error-theory variants deny any commitment or practical role that could ground sincere answerability, restrict the proposal to regret and repair behavior or reject the apology claim.
tests.primary_source_coverage_required: full or clearly bounded excerpts, with exact passages and limits

tests.question: Does sincere apology necessarily assert or presuppose objective moral wrongness, or can acknowledgment, regret, and undertaking have separable force?
tests.method: Compare primary accounts of apology and speech-act sincerity against explicit cases where the speaker disavows objective moral wrongness but truthfully acknowledges the act and offers repair.
tests.result_that_supports_claim: A defensible account allows some apologies to be sincere without belief in objective moral wrongness, even if some apology forms require that belief.
tests.result_that_narrows_or_defeats_claim: If objective moral avowal is necessary for sincerity in ordinary apology, narrow the claim to sincere apology-like commitments or reject it.

tests.question: Can the recipient's role in an accountability undertaking be described without quietly reinstating objective moral authority?
tests.method: List every normative-sounding step in the worked case (standing, demand, repair, promise, answerability); distinguish objective entitlement, agreement-based role, and chosen policy; attempt to construct a global-error-theory countermodel.
tests.result_that_supports_claim: The speaker can sincerely commit to a practice role while explicitly denying that the role proves a categorical moral right.
tests.result_that_narrows_or_defeats_claim: If any intelligible apology requires objective authority or a genuine normative reason that the global error theorist denies, exclude the global variant or reject it as an apology account.

tests.question: Does the undertaking remain recognizable as an apology when the recipient may insist on moral acknowledgment?
tests.method: Analyze paired cases with identical repair behavior but different speaker avowals and recipient conditions. Separate speaker sincerity, apology adequacy, and relationship repair; do not treat hypothetical or model ratings as evidence of truth.
tests.result_that_supports_claim: At least some case has a sincere accountability apology even though a recipient could reasonably reject it as inadequate.
tests.result_that_narrows_or_defeats_claim: If all transparent no-avowal cases are only promises, concessions, or damage control, narrow the conclusion to those practices rather than apology.

tests.question: Is the avowal–undertaking distinction already made by the closest work on error theory, fictionalism, expressivism, apology, and practical commitment?
tests.method: Search and read relevant primary texts across those traditions; compare exact claims, not just vocabulary, and preserve search queries, source bytes, excerpts, and unavailable items in a separate source stage.
tests.result_that_supports_claim: A distinct and defensible boundary test remains after comparison with closest arguments.
tests.result_that_narrows_or_defeats_claim: If a close source already establishes the same distinction and test, identify the contribution as derivative or set it aside unless a new argument survives.

tests.question: Can the proposal distinguish sincere accountability from strategic appeasement when the speaker would not repair absent reputational or relational benefit?
tests.method: Vary the speaker's incentives while holding the stated apology constant; specify what intentions and subsequent actions sincerity requires and test whether the definition is circular.
tests.result_that_supports_claim: Sincerity can be tied to a stable intention to perform the undertaking rather than to obtaining forgiveness or advantage.
tests.result_that_narrows_or_defeats_claim: If no non-circular difference between genuine undertaking and strategic display can be stated, the sincerity claim is unsupported.
